answer: To validate identity, an agent pins a 64 GB lookup table into sable DRAM channels. The verifier then issues sequential, non-cacheable pointer-chasing probes restricted to a 60-nanosecond bus access budget. Genuine hardware reads form a predictable mesa of flat latency, whereas serialized or shared storage plunges query rates to an unrecoverable nadir. Any timed-out hop prompts the verifier to reject the proof and burn the node's 500-token bond, making multi-identity simulation prohibitively expensive.
